title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON SUPPORT FOR PERSONS ELIGIBLE FOR VETERANS' COMPENSATION
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters mandated by the Act on Support for Persons Eligible for Veterans' Compensation and matters necessary for the enforcement thereof.

Article 2 (Criteria for, and scope of, requirements for persons eligible for veterans' compensation) (1) The criteria for, and scope of, requirements for persons eligible for veterans' compensation under Article 2(2) of the Act on Support for Persons Eligible for Veterans' Compensation (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") shall be as follows: <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020; Dec. 30, 2022>
  1. A person specified in Article 2(1)1 and 2 of the Act: A deceased or wounded person specified in any of subparagraphs 1 through 17 of Appendix 1;
  2. A person specified in Article 2(1)3 and 4 of the Act: A deceased or wounded person specified in any of subparagraphs 1 through 7, 10, 11, or 15 of Appendix 1.
  (2) The medical determination of whether the onset or aggravation of the relevant disease has a substantial causal relationship with the performance of duties or participation in education and training, as prescribed in subparagraph 11 of Appendix 1, shall be based on a comprehensive consideration of the following records, circumstances, and other relevant factors: <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020; Jan. 5, 2021; May 23, 2023>
  1. Medical certificates, autopsy reports (documents confirming the medical fact of death), certificates, prescriptions, clinical opinions, medical records, or nursing records under Article 17, 17-2, 21, or 22 of the Medical Service Act; and other records related to medical treatment under medical service-related statutes or regulations, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs;
  2. Working conditions, the duration of service, the nature of duties, and the conditions present at the time the duties are performed;
  3. Whether the relevant deceased person or the person suffering from a disease had the disease previously.
  (3) The criteria for, and scope of, major diseases falling under subparagraph 11 of Appendix 1 and the requirements for persons eligible for veterans' compensation for each major disease shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 3 (Employees routinely engaged in public service for the State) "Employee prescribed by Presidential Decree who routinely engages in public service for the State or a local government" in Article 2(1)3 or 4 or 72(1)4 of the Act means a person subject to Article 2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Public Officials Pension.

Article 4 (Persons with disabilities to extent of being incapable of supporting themselves) "Person with a disability to the extent of being incapable of supporting oneself, as prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the provisions, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 3(5) of the Act and paragraph (6) of that Article means a person with a mental or physical disability as classified in the Disability Classification Table for Persons with Disabilities specified in Appendix 2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State. In such cases, the classification of a disability for a person with a disability shall be determined by applying mutatis mutandis the provisions regarding new physical examinations and physical re-examinations under Article 6-3 of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State.

Article 5 (Application for registration) (1) To be registered as a person eligible for veterans' compensation or as a family member of such person, whether bereaved or not, pursuant to Article 4(1) of the Act, an application for registration shall be filed by a person with priority in the following order (if the highest-priority bereaved family member is unable to file such application due to unavoidable circumstances, referring to other bereaved family members specified in the subparagraphs of Article 3(1) of the Act) with the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, along with the documents prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs: <Amended on Dec. 31, 2018; May 23, 2023>
  1. A person eligible for veterans' compensation or his or her bereaved family members with priority under Article 12 of the Act;
  2. Bereaved family members who do not fall under the category specified in subparagraph 1 shall have the priority established under the subparagraphs of Article 3(1) of the Act, and if they are in the same priority group, they shall follow the order established under Article 12 of the Act.
  (2) "Case prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso of Article 4(4) of the Act means where the status requirements of a person eligible for veterans' compensation and his or her family members, whether bereaved or not, are verified based on official records, such as a certificate of family relations records or a certified copy of archived family register.

Article 6 (Notification of verification of facts related to requirements for persons eligible for veterans' compensation) (1) "Head of an agency to which the relevant person belonged" in the latter part of Article 4(3) of the Act shall be classified as follows: <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; Dec. 4, 2013; Nov. 19, 2014; Nov. 20, 2015; Jul. 26, 2017; Sep. 18, 2018; Jun. 30, 2020>
  1. In cases of a member of the National Assembly: The Secretary General of the National Assembly;
  2. In cases of a police officer or auxiliary police officer: The Commissioner General of the Korean National Police Agency or the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard;
  3. In cases of a soldier: The Minister of National Defense;
  4. In cases of a firefighting official or obligatory firefighting unit member: The Fire Commissioner of the National Fire Agency;
  5. In cases of a public official other than those specified in subparagraphs 1 through 4: The following persons:
  a. In cases of a public official who files an application for approval for convalescence for official purpose or claims disability benefits under Article 28 or 41 of the Enforcement Decree of the Public Officials’ Accident Compensation Act: The Minister of Personnel Management;
  b. In cases of a public official who fails to file an application for approval for convalescence for official purpose or to claim disability benefits under Article 28 or 41 of the Enforcement Decree of the Public Officials’ Accident Compensation Act (including a public official not subject to the Public Officials’ Accident Compensation Act): The head of an agency in which the relevant public official held an office at the time he or she died or suffered wounds (including a disease);
  6. In cases of a member of social service personnel: The Commissioner of the Military Manpower Administration;
  7. In cases of a member of alternative service personnel: The Minister of Justice.
  (2) If the head of an agency under paragraph (1) (hereinafter referred to as the "head of an agency to which a person belonged") receives an application for verification as to whether the requirements specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2(1) of the Act are met from the relevant wounded person, his or her family, or a bereaved family of a deceased person, or receives a request for the verification thereof from the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, the head shall verify the fact related to such requirements and notify, without delay, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affair of the fact. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (3) When the head of an agency to which the relevant person belonged notifies the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs pursuant to paragraph (2), the head shall submit a written verification of the fact related to the requirements for a person eligible for veteran's compensation in the form prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans, along with a medical certificate, a medical record, and other documents evidencing the fact related to the requirements for a person eligible for veteran's compensation (in cases of a public official specified in paragraph (1)5a, including a written investigation of the details of wounds or disease and a copy of written determination of approval for medical care related to the performance of official duties under Article 28 of the Enforcement Decree of the Public Officials' Accident Compensation Act; a written investigation of the details of a disability under Article 41 of that Decree; or a written investigation of the details of death under Article 50 of that Decree). <Amended on Sep. 18, 2018; May 23, 2023>
  (4) Where the head of an agency to which the relevant person belonged has provided notification under paragraph (2), the head shall inform a person who intends to be registered as a person eligible for veterans' compensation or his or her family, whether bereaved or not, of the procedures for filing an application for registration and for the examination thereof.
  (5) Upon receipt of notification under paragraph (2) from the head of an agency to which the relevant person belonged, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall, without delay, refer the relevant case to the Patriots and Veterans Entitlement Commission established under Article 74- 5 of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State (hereinafter referred to as the "Patriots and Veterans Entitlement Commission") for deliberation. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 7 (Examination of requirements for eligibility for veterans' compensation and determination of such eligibility) (1) Upon receipt of an application for registration under Article 5(1) or a referral under Article 6(5), the Patriots and Veterans Entitlement Commission shall deliberate and resolve on whether the requirements for eligibility for veterans' compensation are met.
  (2) The Patriots and Veterans Entitlement Commission shall notify the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, without delay, of the result under paragraph (1). <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (3) Upon receipt of notification under paragraph (2), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall determine whether the relevant person is subject to the application of the Act and shall notify such determination to the applicant and the head of the agency to which the relevant person belonged, specifying the reasons therefor; provided, for a person who meets the requirements for a person who has suffered an injury as prescribed in Article 2(1)2 or 4 of the Act and whose eligibility is determined and resolved on by the Patriots and Veterans Entitlement Commission, whether the person is subject to the application of the Act shall be determined after conducting a physical examination and determining his or her injury grade. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 8 (Physical examinations and determination of injury grades) `Articles 13 through 19 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State shall apply mutatis mutandis to physical examinations and determination of injury grades for persons eligible for veterans' compensation under Article 6 of the Act.

CHAPTER II VETERANS' BENEFITS

Article 9 (Allowances) "Allowances prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 10(2)5 of the Act means the following allowances:
  1. Old age allowances;
  2. Allowances for at least 2 deceased persons.

Article 10 (Compensation) Compensation shall be paid to persons eligible for veterans' compensation and their bereaved family members under Article 11(1) and (2) of the Act according to the payment classification specified in Appendix 2.

Article 11 (Injury grades of soldiers or police officers wounded in disasters eligible for bereaved family's compensations) "Injury grade prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 11(1)3 of the Act means Injury Grade VI.

Article 12 (Mental or physical disabilities to extent of being incapable of supporting oneself) "Disability to the extent of being incapable of supporting oneself as prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Articles 11(2) and 18(3) of the Act means a mental or physical disability as classified in the Disability Classification Table for Persons with Disabilities specified in Appendix 2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State.

Article 13 (Methods of designating compensation recipients through consultation and effect thereof) (1) A person who intends to receive compensation through consultation among bereaved family members pursuant to Article 12(2)1 of the Act shall submit, through such consultation, a written designation of a compensation recipient in the form prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, along with the certificates of seal impressions of all bereaved family members in the same order of priority (if any such family member is a minor, referring to the certificate of the seal impression of his or her legal representative); provided, in any unavoidable cases where the submission of such written designation is impossible, such as where any bereaved family member in the same order of priority resides abroad, a notarial deed under the Notary Public Act indicating that the person was designated as a compensation recipient may be submitted in lieu of the designation. <Amended on Dec. 24, 2019; May 23, 2023>
  (2) The effect of consultation under Article 12(2)1 of the Act shall not be altered by the will of one party alone; provided, even if one of the parents of a person eligible for veterans' compensation is designated as a person to receive compensation through consultation, the effect of consultation for such designation shall be nullified if either parent applies for the payment of compensation in equal portions under Article 12(2)3 of the Act. <Added on Dec. 24, 2019>
  [Title Amended on Dec. 24, 2019]
  [Moved from Article 14; previous Article 13 moved to Article 14 <Dec. 24, 2019>]

Article 14 (Payment of compensation to those who have primarily supported or raised persons eligible for veterans' compensation) (1) If a person intends to receive compensation as a person who has primarily supported or raised a person eligible for veterans' compensation pursuant to Article 12(2)2 of the Act, the person shall submit documents proving such fact, to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on Dec. 24, 2019; May 23, 2023>
  (2) If a dispute arises among bereaved family members in the same priority order while proving that they have primarily supported or raised a person eligible for veterans' compensation pursuant to paragraph (1), the person to receive compensation shall be determined after deliberation and resolution by the Patriots and Veterans Entitlement Commission.
  [Moved from Article 13; previous Article 14 moved to Article 13 <Dec. 24, 2019>]

Article 14-2 (Application for payment of compensation in equal portions by parents of persons eligible for veterans' compensation) (1) A parent of a person eligible for veterans' compensation who intends to receive compensation divided equally pursuant to Article 12(2)3 of the Act shall submit an application for the payment of such compensation, etc. in equal portions in the form prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) Except as provided in paragraph (1), necessary matters regarding the methods and procedures for the payment of compensation in equal portions to the parents of persons eligible for veterans' compensation shall be prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  [This Article Added on Dec. 24, 2019]

Article 15 (Livelihood improvement allowances) (1) Livelihood improvement allowances under Article 13 of the Act shall be paid to persons meeting the criteria determined and publicly notified by the Minister based on the standard cost of living of the general public, the fluctuations in wages and in the prices of goods and services in the private sector, and other relevant factors, in accordance with the payment classification specified in Appendix 3. <Amended on Dec, 24, 2019; May 23, 2023>
  (2) If a person eligible for livelihood improvement allowances under paragraph (1) is a parent of a person eligible for veterans' compensation, the livelihood improvement allowances in accordance with the payment classification specified in Appendix 3 may be paid in equal portions. In such cases, a parent of a person eligible for veterans' compensation who intends to receive the livelihood improvement allowances in equal portions shall submit an application for the payment of compensation, etc. in equal portions in the form prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Added on Dec. 24, 2019; May 23, 2023>

Article 16 (Application for payment of livelihood improvement allowances) (1) A person who intends to receive livelihood improvement allowances pursuant to Article 14(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "person seeking to receive livelihood improvement allowances") shall submit an application for payment in the form prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, along with relevant documents, such as a means test report. <Amended on May 23, 2023; Aug. 6, 2024>
  (2) "Causes prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as mobility impairment" in Article 14(3)2 of the Act means any of the following causes: <Added on Aug. 6, 2024>
  1. Where the relevant person experiences mobility impairment;
  2. Where the relevant person is hospitalized or under long-term medical care due to a disease or injury, etc.;
  3. Where the relevant person has been assigned an injury grade based on a physical examination under Article 6 of the Act (applicable only to persons eligible for veterans' compensation);
  4. Where the relevant person is at least 65 years of age or under 19 years of age.
  (3) A public official in charge may obtain consent to a proxy application by a public official in charge under Article 14(3)3 of the Act, by any of the following methods: <Added on Aug. 6, 2024>
  1. Notifying a person seeking to receive livelihood improvement allowances of a document stating that the person consents to a proxy application by a public official in charge, by mail, fax, email, or other similar means; and receiving a written consent signed or sealed by the person;
  2. Notifying a person seeking to receive livelihood improvement allowances of the details of consent to a proxy application by a public official in charge by phone, confirming the person's consent to such application, and recording such fact in writing, by video recording, or by other similar means.
  (4) Except as provided in paragraph (1), matters necessary for the methods and procedures for filing applications for livelihood improvement allowances shall be prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023; Aug. 6, 2024>
  [Title Amended on Aug. 6, 2024]

Article 16-2 (Scope of household members) `Article 25-3 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State shall apply mutatis mutandis to a person falling under the category of household members specified in the provisions, with the exception of the subparagraphs of, Article 14(2) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "household members").
  [This Article Added on Apr. 1, 2025]

Article 17 (Scope of financial information) (1) "Average bank balance and other data or information or data prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 14(2)1 of the Act means the following data or information:
  1. Demand deposits, such as ordinary deposits, savings accounts, and free savings accounts: The average balance within the last 3 months;
  2. Savings deposits, such as term deposits, term installment deposits, and term savings deposits: The balance or total amount of deposits;
  3. Shares, beneficiary certificates, investments, equity stakes, and real estate (annuity) trusts: The final market value; in such cases, Article 54(1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Inheritance Tax and Gift Tax Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the valuation of unlisted shares;
  4. Bonds, bills, checks, certificates of debenture, certificates of preemptive right to new stocks, and certificates of deposit: The face value;
  5. Pension savings: The regularly paid amount or the final balance.
  (2) "Amount of debts and other data or information prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 14(2)2 of the Act means the following data or information:
  1. Loan status and details of arrearage;
  2. Unpaid credit card amount.
  (3) "Insurance premiums ... and other data or information prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 14(2)3 of the Act means the following data or information:
  1. Insurance policies: The refund payable upon contract termination or the insurance benefits paid within the most recent year;
  2. Pension insurance: The refund payable upon contract termination or the regularly paid amount.
  (4) Matters necessary for submitting documents confirming consent to the provision of financial information under paragraph (1), credit information under paragraph (2), and insurance information under paragraph (3) (hereinafter referred to as "financial information, etc.") shall be prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 18 (Investigations for verification) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall formulate an annual investigation plan each year, which shall include the following to verify whether persons seeking to receive livelihood improvement allowances, recipients of such allowances (referring to any person specified in the subparagraphs of Article 13(1) of the Act who receive such allowances; hereinafter the same shall apply), and their household members have obtained or forfeited the entitlement to the allowances: <Amended on May 23, 2023; Apr. 1, 2025>
  1. The basic direction for investigations;
  2. The scope, details, and timing of, and the procedures for, investigations and inquiries; and the measures for establishing a system for cooperation in obtaining materials;
  3. Other matters necessary to conduct means tests for persons seeking to receive livelihood improvement allowances, recipients of such allowances, and their household members.

Article 19 (Request for, and provision of, financial information) (1) When the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs requests that the head of a financial company, etc. (including a financial company defined in subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality and a centralized credit information collection agency permitted under Article 25(2)1 of the Credit Information Use and Protection Act) provide financial information, etc. on a person seeking to receive livelihood improvement allowances, a recipient of such allowances, and their household members pursuant to Article 16 of the Act, the Minister shall include the following in the requested details: <Amended on Aug. 4, 2020; May 23, 2023; Apr. 1, 2025>
  1. The names and resident registration numbers of a person seeking to receive livelihood improvement allowances, a recipient of such allowances, and their household members;
  2. The scope of the requested financial information, etc., the base date of inquiry, and the inquiry period.
  (2) When the head of a financial company, etc. provide the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs with the relevant financial information, etc. upon receipt of a request under paragraph (1), the head shall include the following in the information provided: <Amended on May 23, 2023; Apr. 1, 2025>
  1. The names and resident registration numbers of a person seeking to receive livelihood improvement allowances, a recipient of such allowances, and their household members;
  2. The name of a financial company, etc., that provide the financial information, etc.;
  3. The name and account number of a financial product subject to information provision;
  4. The details of the financial information, etc.
  (3) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may request the head of a financial company, etc. to provide financial information, etc. through an information and communications network of an association, a federation, a national federation, or a similar organization in which the relevant financial company, etc. have a membership. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (4) When the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs requests the head of a finance company, etc. to provide financial information, etc. on a recipient of livelihood improvement allowances and his or her household members pursuant to Article 16(2) of the Act, the Minister shall request only the minimum financial information, etc. necessary to verify entitlement to such allowances. <Amended on May 23, 2023; Apr. 1, 2025>

Article 20 (Nursing allowances) The standards for paying nursing allowances under Article 17 of the Act and the amounts to be paid shall be as specified in Appendix 4.

Article 21 (Allowances for dependents) (1) "Injury grade prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 18(1)1 of the Act means Injury Grade VII. <Amended on Jan. 6, 2026>
  (2) Allowances for dependents shall be paid to any person specified in the subparagraphs of Article 18(1) of the Act in accordance with the payment classification specified in Appendix 5.

Article 22 (Additional allowances for severe injuries) (1) "Injury grade prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 19(1) of the Act means Injury Grade I.
  (2) The monthly payment amount of additional allowances for severe injuries under Article 19 of the Act shall be as follows: <Amended on Jan. 14, 2013; Jan. 12, 2015; Jan. 7, 2016; Dec. 30, 2016; Dec. 29, 2017; Dec. 31, 2018; Jan. 7, 2020; Jan. 5, 2021; Jan. 13, 2022; Jan. 13, 2023; Jan. 12, 2024; Jan. 14, 2025; Jan. 6, 2026>
  1. A person assigned Injury Grade I-1: 2,131,000 won;
  2. A person assigned Injury Grade I-2: 1,473,000 won;
  3. A person assigned Injury Grade I-3: 898,000 won.

Article 23 (Payment standards for old age allowances and allowance for at least 2 deceased persons) (1) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall pay allowances specified in the subparagraphs of Article 9 to a person eligible for compensation under Article 11(1) and (2) of the Act according to the payment classification specified in Appendix 6; provided, if each parent of a person eligible for veterans' compensation, who receives compensation in equal portions pursuant to Article 12(2)3 of the Act, is eligible for the payment of allowances specified in Appendix 6, the Minister shall pay such allowances in equal portions to them. <Amended on Nov. 20, 2018; Dec. 24, 2019; May 23, 2023>
  (2) No old age allowance under subparagraph 1 of Article 9 shall be paid to a person eligible for the following allowances: <Amended on Jan. 13, 2022>
  1. Allowances for dependents under Article 10(2)3 of the Act;
  2. Allowances for at least 2 deceased persons under subparagraph 2 of Article 9;
  3. Allowances for at least 2 deceased persons referred to in Article 23(1)2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State, and in subparagraph 5 of Appendix specified in Article 10(1) of the Addenda to the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State (Presidential decree no. 23885).
  (3) Notwithstanding paragraph (2), if an allowance for dependents under Article 10(2)3 of the Act is less than an old age allowance under subparagraph 1 of Article 9, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall pay an old age allowance equivalent to the difference. <Added on Jan. 13, 2022; May 23, 2023>

Article 24 (Lump-sum payment on death) (1) The amounts of lump-sum payment on death under Article 20 of the Act shall be as specified in Appendix 7.
  (2) A person who intends to receive a lump-sum payment on death under paragraph (1) shall submit an application for lump-sum payment on death to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, along with the documents prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 24-2 (Reasons for cash payments of veterans' benefits) "Unavoidable circumstance prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as damage to information and communications networks" in the proviso of Article 20-2(1) of the Act means any of the following cases: <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  1. Where a post office or a bank at which an account for depositing veterans' benefits (referring to an account opened at a post office under the postal savings and insurance act (hereinafter referred to as "post office") or a bank under the Banking Act (hereinafter referred to as "bank"); hereinafter the same shall apply) is opened, is unable to conduct its normal business operations due to the permanent closure or suspension of the business operations, an information and communication system failure, or any other similar event, making it impossible to transfer veterans' benefits;
  2. Where the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs deems the cash payment of veterans' benefits unavoidable.
  [This Article Added on Jun. 21, 2016]

Article 25 (Payment dates of veterans' benefits) (1) Compensation, livelihood improvement allowances, nursing allowances, allowances for dependents, and additional allowances for severe injuries under Articles 11, 13, 17, 18, and 19 of the Act, as well as allowances under Article 9 shall be paid on the 15th day of each month; provided, if the payment date of veterans' benefits falls on a Saturday or public holiday, the benefits shall be paid on the preceding day.
  (2) In special circumstances, such as a natural disaster, accident, or any other similar situation, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may separately determine the payment date of veterans' benefits, notwithstanding paragraph (1). <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (3) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), an overseas resident who receives remittances of veterans' benefits may be paid the benefits for the period from January to December in a lump sum in December. <Amended on Nov. 11, 2014>

Article 26 (Unpaid veterans' benefits) A person who intends to receive unpaid veterans' benefits pursuant to Article 21 of the Act shall submit an application for the payment of unpaid veterans' benefits to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, along with the documents prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs; provided, if the information in the attached documents can be verified through administrative data matching under Article 36(1) of the Electronic Government Act, such verification shall substitute for the attached documents. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 26-2 (Amount of veterans' benefits prohibited from seizure or attachment) "Amount not exceeding the amount prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 22(3) of the Act means the total amount of monthly veterans' benefits deposited pursuant to Article 20-2(2) of the Act.
  [This Article Added on Jun. 21, 2016]

Article 27 (Methods of paying veterans' benefits) (1) Article 20-2(1) of the Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the methods of paying any of the following grants, etc.: <Amended on Jun. 21, 2016>
  1. Grants under Article 29 of the Act;
  2. Subsidies under Article 30 of the Act;
  3. Learning allowances under Article 31 of the Act;
  4. Expenses incurred in providing vocational rehabilitation training and vocational skills development training under Article 48 of the Act;
  5. Subsidies for skills development and incentives under Article 49 of the Act;
  6. Subsidies for medical expenses under Article 51 of the Act.
  (2) Veterans' benefits, etc. deposited in the account of a person entitled to receive veterans' benefits under Article 10 of the Act and grants, etc. under the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) (hereinafter referred to as "veterans' benefits") shall be deemed received by the person; provided, if veterans' benefits, etc., were deposited in the account of a person whose entitlement to receive such benefits lapsed due to changes in any personal circumstances specified in Article 5(1)1 through 7 of the Act, and the person fails to collect all or some of the veterans' benefits, etc.; the veterans' benefits, etc. shall be deemed not received by the person. <Amended on Jun. 21, 2016>
  (3) In the case of the proviso of paragraph (2), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may cancel the deposit. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 28 (Verification of persons eligible for veterans' benefits) If it is necessary to verify whether a person who receives veterans' benefits, etc. is entitled to receive such benefits, etc., the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may request the head of a Si/Gun/Gu (the head of a Gu refers to the head of an autonomous Gu) or the Jeju Special Self-Governing Province Governor to verify the identity of the person at least once a year, and the head of the relevant agency receiving such request shall without delay conduct an investigation and notify the result. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 29 (Designation of authorized recipients) If a person entitled to receive veterans' benefits is unable to receive such benefits due to illness, residing overseas, or any other unavoidable cause, the person shall submit an application for approval of the designation of an authorized recipient to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, along with the documents prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs and shall obtain the designation of the authorized recipient. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 30 (Standards for amount of compensation to be suspended from payment) "Amount ... prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 23 of the Act means the amount specified in Appendix 7-2.
  [This Article Added on Mar. 5, 2024]

CHAPTER III EDUCATIONAL ASSISTANCE

Article 31 (Educational assistance based on standards of living) (1) "Injury grade prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 25(3) of the Act means Injury Grade VI.
  (2) Educational assistance shall be provided to a person falling under Article 25(3) of the Act, only if the person meets the criteria determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, based on the standard cost of living of the general public, the fluctuations in wages and in the prices of goods and services in the private sector, and other relevant factors. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (3) A person who intends to apply for educational assistance pursuant to the former part of Article 25(4) of the Act shall submit an application for educational assistance to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, along with the documents prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 32 (Adjustment of school admission ratio) (1) If the number of persons eligible for educational assistance in each region who are to attend high schools and other equivalent schools exceeds the school admission ratio under Article 27(1) of the Act, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall notify the Minister of Education of the number of such persons in the relevant region. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013; May 23, 2023>
  (2) Upon receipt of notification under paragraph (1), the Minister of Education shall determine the school admission ratio for each Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, Special Self-Governing Province, or Si/Gun pursuant to Article 27(2) of the Act and shall notify the superintendent of education of the relevant Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Special Self-Governing City, or Special Self-Governing Province (hereafter in this chapter referred to as "superintendent of education of a City/Do") of the ratio at least 10 days prior to the entrance examination. <Amended on Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 33 (Verification of persons eligible for educational assistance) (1) If a person eligible for educational assistance seeks admission to a middle or high school or any other equivalent school, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall verify the eligibility of the person at the request of the head of a district office of education, the superintendent of education of a City/Do, or the principal of a school that has received an application for allotment or admission. <Amended on Nov. 11, 2014; May 23, 2023>
  (2) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall prepare a list of applicants seeking admission to a middle or high school who are persons eligible for educational assistance under paragraph (1) and shall submit the list to the head of the competent district office of education for middle school admission applicants or to the superintendent of education of the competent City/Do for high school admission applicants. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  [Title Amended on Nov. 11, 2014]

Article 34 (Admission determination for persons eligible for educational assistance) The determination of whether to grant admission to a person eligible for educational assistance who intends to attend a high school and any other equivalent school shall be as determined by the superintendent of education of a City/Do.

Article 35 (Notification of admission determination for persons eligible for educational assistance) The head of a district office of education or the superintendent of education of a City/Do shall notify the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs of the list of persons eligible for educational assistance whose admission to a middle or high school or any other equivalent school within the relevant jurisdiction has been determined. <Amended on Jun. 21, 2016; May 23, 2023>

Article 36 (Transfer) (1) If a person eligible for educational assistance who attends a middle or high school intends to transfer to another school, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall verify the eligibility of the person for such assistance, at the request of the head of a district office of education, the superintendent of education of a City/Do, or the principal of a school who has received an application for transfer. <Amended on Nov. 11, 2014; May 23, 2023>
  (2) Deleted. <Nov. 11, 2014>
  (3) If the eligibility for educational assistance is verified pursuant to paragraph (1), the head of the competent district office of education or the superintendent of education of the competent City/Do shall assign the person eligible for educational assistance to a school district adjacent to his or her place of residence, ensuring that the school admission ratio for persons eligible for educational assistance does not exceed the specified limit for the relevant grade. <Amended on Nov. 11, 2014>

Article 37 (Notification of school attendance status) If any changes in school attendance status, such as expulsion, suspension, or temporary absence from school, or return to school, involve a person eligible for educational assistance, the head of an educational institution specified in the subparagraphs of Article 26 of the Act or the principal of a foreigners' school, etc. specified in the subparagraphs of Article 30(1) of the Act shall submit a notice of changes in school attendance status to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs within 10 days from the date the relevant reason arises. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 38 (Exemption from tuition fees and procedures for exemption) (1) If any person specified in the subparagraphs of Article 25(1) of the Act attends any educational institution specified in the subparagraphs of Article 26 of the Act, the person shall be exempt from tuition fees, etc. under Article 29(1) of the Act (including admission fees and school operating assistance expenses for a middle or high school; hereinafter the same shall apply). <Amended on Jun. 21, 2016>
  (2) The fixed period of exemption from tuition fees, etc. for persons eligible for educational assistance shall be as follows: <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  1. For a person eligible for educational assistance who falls under the category specified in Article 25(1)1 or 2 of the Act, the exemption shall apply until the person completes or graduates from the education institution he or she attends; the same shall also apply if the eligible person is admitted, readmitted, specially admitted, or transferred to the relevant or another educational institution;
  2. For a person eligible for educational assistance who falls under the category specified in Article 25(1)3 or 4 of the Act, the exemption shall apply until the following fixed period:
  a. For a person eligible for educational assistance who attends an educational institution with a prescribed period of study: The exemption shall apply within a prescribed period of study (excluding summer and winter sessions within the period) prescribed by education-related statutes or regulations or by the school regulations of the relevant educational institution; provided, if the eligible person is admitted, readmitted, specially admitted, or transferred to the relevant or another educational institution, the person shall be exempt from tuition fees, etc. for the remaining prescribed period of study at the current school, excluding the prescribed period of study for which the person was already exempt from tuition fees, etc. at a former school;
  b. For a person eligible for educational assistance who attends an educational institution without a prescribed period of study: The exemption shall apply within a prescribed period determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs.
  (3) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), tuition fees, etc. shall not be exempted for a person eligible for educational assistance who falls under the category specified in Article 25(1)3 or 4, from among those who attend the following educational institutions under the proviso of Article 29(2) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "university, etc."), if the person has obtained an average score below 70 percent of the perfect score in the immediately preceding semester, or if the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs or the president of the relevant university, etc. deems that the person has damaged the dignity of a family member, whether bereaved or not, of a person eligible for veterans' compensation: <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  1. A university or college specified in subparagraph 2 of Article 26 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "university");
  2. A lifelong educational facility in the form of an online university and an educational or training institution that operates a course of study, the credits of which are recognized as part of the credits required to obtain a degree of a junior college or higher, among educational institutions specified in subparagraphs 3 and 4 of Article 26 of the Act.
  (4) If any of the following persons eligible for educational assistance intends to be exempt from tuition fees, etc. under Article 29(1) of the Act, the person shall submit his or her certificate of eligibility for educational assistance issued by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs to the head of the relevant educational institution; provided, if the Minister verifies the eligibility of such person for educational assistance pursuant to Article 33(1) or 36 (1), the person need not submit such certificate: <Amended on Nov. 11, 2014; May 23, 2023>
  1. A person who falls under the category specified in Article 25(1)1 or 2 of the Act and attends an educational institution under Article 26 of the Act;
  2. A person who falls under the category specified in Article 25(1)3 or 4 of the Act and attends an educational institution specified in subparagraph 1 of Article 26 of the Act or a lifelong educational facility specified in subparagraph 3 of that Article (applicable only to such facility that offers middle and high school-level programs).
  (5) If a person falling under the category specified in Article 25(1)3 or 4 of the Act intends to be exempt from tuition fees, etc. of a university, etc., the person shall submit his or her certificate of eligibility for exemption from university tuition fees, etc., issued by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, to the president of the relevant university, etc. by the payment deadline for tuition fees, etc. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (6) The president of a private university, etc. who intends to receive subsidies equivalent to half the tuition fees, etc. exempted pursuant to Article 29(3) of the Act shall submit an application for payment of subsidies to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, along with the academic records of the children, etc. of persons eligible for veterans' compensation. Upon receipt of such application, the Minister shall verify the details of the application and determine whether to grant the subsidies and shall notify the president of the relevant private university, etc. of the result. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (7) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may request the president of a university, etc. who has exempted tuition fees, etc. for a person falling under the categories specified in Article 25(1) of the Act to submit the academic records or other necessary materials to verify the exemption. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (8) If a university, etc. are required to exempt tuition fees, etc. for a certain percentage of students under other statutes or regulations, the exemption of tuition fees, etc. provided by the relevant university, etc. pursuant to Article 29(1) of the Act may be deemed to be provided under such other statutes or regulations.

Article 39 (Subsidization of tuition fees and procedures therefor) (1) A person who intends to receive subsidies for tuition fees, etc. pursuant to Article 29(4) of the Act shall submit an application for the payment of tuition fees, etc. in the form prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, along with a receipt of the payment of tuition fees, etc. or a document evidencing such payment and an academic transcript (applicable only to university students). Upon receipt of such application, the Minister shall verify the details of the application and determine whether to provide subsidies. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) "Ground prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso of Article 29(4) of the Act means any of the following cases: <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  1. Where the average score in the immediately preceding semester under Article 38(3) is below 70 percent of the perfect score;
  2. Where the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs or the head of the relevant university, etc. deems that the dignity of a family member, whether bereaved or not, of a person eligible for veterans' compensation has been damaged;
  3. Where an amount equivalent to tuition fees, etc. has been reduced, exempted, or provided as a subsidy pursuant to other statutes or regulations.
  (3) If the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs provides subsidies for tuition fees, etc. pursuant to paragraph (1), the Minister may request the head of an educational institution or the head of an institution, an organization, or any similar entity that has provided subsidies for tuition fees, etc. to submit necessary materials to verify the tuition fees, etc. actually borne by a person eligible for educational assistance. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 40 (Criteria for payment of subsidies to persons eligible for educational assistance attending foreigners' schools, amounts of subsidies, and fixed period of subsidization) (1) A person eligible for educational assistance who attends any foreigners' school, etc. specified in the subparagraphs of Article 30(1) of the Act shall be paid subsidies according to the payment classification specified in Appendix 8; provided, if such subsidies exceed the tuition fees, etc. of the relevant school, the subsidies shall be paid after deducting the excess.
  (2) If a person eligible for educational assistance who attends any foreigners' school, etc. specified in the subparagraphs of Article 30(1) of the Act is granted a reduction of, exemption from, or subsidies for, tuition fees, etc. under other statutes or regulations, the subsidies under paragraph (1) shall be paid after deducting an amount equivalent thereto.
  (3) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), if a person eligible for educational assistance who attends a foreign educational institution equivalent to a university among those specified in Article 30(1)2 of the Act falls under any of the following categories, subsidies for part of tuition fees, etc. shall not be paid: <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  1. Where the average score in the immediately preceding semester is below 70 percent of the perfect score;
  2. Where the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs or the head of the relevant foreign educational institution deems that the dignity of a family member, whether bereaved or not, of a person eligible for veterans' compensation has been damaged.
  (4) The fixed period for the payment of subsidies to persons eligible for educational assistance who attend any foreigners' school, etc. specified in the subparagraphs of Article 30(1) of the Act shall be as follows:
  1. A foreign educational institution equivalent to a middle or high school under Article 2 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, among foreigners' schools specified in Article 30(1)1 of the Act and foreign educational institutions specified in subparagraph 2 of that paragraph: The prescribed period of study provided in Articles 42 and 46 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act;
  2. A foreign educational institution equivalent to universities among those specified in Article 30(1)2 of the Act: The prescribed period of study provided in Article 31(1)1 of the Higher Education Act.
  (5) A person who intends to receive subsidies for tuition fees, etc. pursuant to Article 30 of the Act shall submit an application for the payment of subsidies for tuition fees, etc. of a foreign educational institution in the form prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, along with a receipt of the payment of tuition fees, etc. or a document evidencing such payment and an academic transcript (applicable only to university students). <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (6) Subsidies under paragraph (1) shall be paid on a semester basis according to the academic terms determined by any foreigners' school, etc. specified in the subparagraphs of Article 30(1) of the Act and matters necessary for the methods and procedures for payment shall be determined by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 41 (Payment of learning allowances and procedures therefor) (1) "Person eligible for educational assistance prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 31(1)2 of the Act means any of the following persons: <Amended on Jan. 13, 2022>
  1. A person who falls under the category specified in Article 25(1)1 or 2 of the Act and attends any educational institution specified in the subparagraphs of Article 26 of the Act or any foreigners' school, etc. specified in the subparagraphs of Article 30(1) of the Act;
  2. A person who falls under the category specified in Article 25(1)3 or 4 of the Act and attends an educational institution specified in subparagraph 1 of Article 26 of the Act, a lifelong educational facility specified in subparagraph 3 of that Article (applicable only to such facility that offers middle and high school-level programs), or any foreigners' school, etc. specified in the subparagraphs of Article 30(1) of the Act (excluding a foreign educational institution equivalent to a university);
  3. A child of a soldier or police officer wounded or killed in a disaster specified in Article 25(1)3 or 4 of the Act (limited to persons under 25 whose parents are both deceased) who attends the following educational institutions:
  a. An educational institution specified in subparagraph 2 of Article 26 of the Act;
  b. An educational institution specified in subparagraph 3 of Article 26 of the Act (limited to lifelong educational facilities that offer university-level programs);
  c. An educational institution specified in subparagraph 4 of Article 26 of the Act;
  d. A foreign educational institution equivalent to a university specified in Article 30(1)2 of the Act.
  (2) Learning allowances under Article 31 of the Act shall be paid in accordance with the payment classification specified in Appendix 9.
  (3) Learning allowances under Article 31 of the Act shall be paid to persons eligible for educational assistance or their guardians twice a year, on April 15 and October 15; provided, if the payment date falls on a Saturday or public holiday, or if a natural disaster, accident, or any other similar cause occurs, the proviso of Article 25(1) and paragraph (2) of that Article shall apply mutatis mutandis to the payment of such allowances.
  (4) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (3), matters necessary for the payment of learning allowances shall be determined by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

CHAPTER IV EMPLOYMENT ASSISTANCE

Article 42 (Number of instances of employment assistance) "Number of instances prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 33(2) of the Act means 3 occurrences.

Article 43 (Scope of manufacturers) "Manufacturers prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso of subparagraph 2 of Article 34 of the Act means enterprises falling under classification numbers 10 through 33 specified in Appendix 9 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State. <Amended on Jun. 21, 2016>

Article 44 (Ranks subject to additional scores in employment examinations) The ranks and classes subject to additional scores in employment examinations under Article 35(5) of the Act shall be as specified in Appendix 8 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State.

Article 45 (Issuance of certificates of eligibility for employment assistance) If a person eligible for employment assistance files an application for certification of his or her eligibility for such assistance to receive additional scores in an employment examination, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall issue a certificate of eligibility for employment assistance. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 46 (Application for employment assistance) A person eligible for employment assistance who intends to receive employment assistance pursuant to Article 36 of the Act shall select one of the following applications and submit it to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, along with his or her curriculum vitae: <Amended on Apr. 28, 2014; Dec. 19, 2017; May 23, 2023; Nov. 12, 2024>
  1. A person eligible for employment assistance who intends to be recommended for special recruitment of a public official in general service or general civilian military employee pursuant to Article 37 of the Act: An application for recommendation for special recruitment of a public official in general service or general civilian military employee;
  2. A person eligible for employment assistance who intends to seek employment in accordance with the special employment policy for veterans under Article 41 of the Act: An application for employment.

Article 47 (Public officials in general service subject to special recruitment) (1) "Public officials in general service and general civilian military employees prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the former part of Article 37(1) of the Act means public officials in general service specified in Appendix 8-2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State and general civilian military employees belonging to the management and operation service group under Appendix 1 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Personnel Management of Civilian Military Employee (hereinafter referred to as "public official in general service, etc."). <Amended on Nov. 12, 2024>
  (2) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall determine the employment ratio at which an agency providing employment assistance falling under the former part of Article 32(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "State agency, etc.") is required to employ persons eligible for employment assistance as public officials in general service, etc. up to 20 percent of the fixed number of public officials in general service, etc., including persons employed under other statutes and regulations related to veterans affairs (referring to statutes and regulations prescribed in subparagraph 3 of Article 3 of the Framework Act on Veterans Affairs; hereafter in Article 50(1), the same shall apply). In such cases, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall consider the number of persons eligible for employment assistance who intend to be employed as public officials in general service, etc. and the opinions of the head of a central personnel agency under Article 6 of the State Public Officials Act and the head of a central administrative agency responsible for the personnel management system of local public officials. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Apr. 28, 2014]

Article 48 (Special recruitment of public officials in general service) (1) If the head of a State agency, etc., that fail to meet the employment ratio under Article 47 (hereinafter referred to as "employment ratio") intends to employ public officials in general service, etc., the head shall request the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs to recommend persons eligible for employment assistance, specifying the number of public officials in general service, etc. to be employed, qualification requirements, etc., and other relevant information, without following the public announcement procedures for employment examinations under the statutes and regulations governing the employment of public officials in general service, etc., including the State Public Officials Act and the Local Public Officials Act (hereinafter referred to as "statutes and regulations related to personnel management"), until the number of persons eligible for employment assistance for the State agency, etc., reaches the number corresponding to the employment ratio.
  (2) Upon receipt of a request for recommendation under paragraph (1), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall, within 7 days from the date of receipt of such request, recommend to the relevant State agency, etc., persons eligible for employment assistance who meet the relevant qualification requirements, in a number up to 5 times the number of persons to be employed as requested by the head of the State agency, etc. in the form of a letter of recommendation of persons eligible for special recruitment of public officials in general service, etc. <Amended on Apr. 28, 2014; May 23, 2023>
  (3) Upon receipt of a recommendation under paragraph (2), the head of the relevant State agency, etc. shall employ persons eligible for employment assistance, as prescribed by statutes and regulations related to personnel management and shall notify the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs of the result in the form of a notice of special recruitment of public officials in general service, etc. <Amended on Apr. 28, 2014; May 23, 2023>
  (4) The head of a State agency, etc. that fail to meet the employment ratio may employ public officials in general service, etc., as prescribed by statutes and regulations related to personnel management, without following the recommendation procedures, etc. under paragraphs (1) through (3), in any of the following cases: <Amended on Apr. 28, 2014; May 23, 2023>
  1. Where an agreement has been reached with the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs to recruit public officials in general service, etc. through a competitive employment examination of experienced persons pursuant to Article 28(2)1 or 3 of the State Public Officials Act and Article 27(2)1 or 3 of the Local Public Officials Act;
  2. Where the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs fails to make a recommendation by the deadline under paragraph (2);
  3. Where an agreement has been reached with the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs due to special reasons prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, such as where it is impracticable for the State agency, etc. to directly administer an employment examination because a separate examination administering agency exists.
  [Title Amended on Apr. 28, 2014]

Article 49 (Notification of current employment conditions of State agencies, etc.) Upon receipt of a request from the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs for the fixed number and the current employment conditions of public officials in general service, etc. and for the result of corrective and supplementary measures, as prescribed in Article 38 of the Act, the head of a State agency, etc. shall notify the Minister within 30 days from the date of receipt such request. In such cases, the notification may be provided in conjunction with a notification under Article 52 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State. <Amended on Apr. 28, 2014; May 23, 2023>

Article 50 (Employment ratios of enterprises) (1) The employment ratio of each target enterprise under Article 39(1) of the Act shall be as specified in Appendix 9 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State, including persons preferentially employed under other statues and regulations related to veterans affairs; provided, the employment ratio for each target enterprise applicable to an institution providing employment assistance specified in the subparagraphs of Article 39(2) of the Act shall be the ratio calculated by adding 1 percent to the employment ratio specified in Appendix 9 of that Decree.
  (2) "Enterprise or organization prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 39(2)3 of the Act means any of the following institutions providing employment assistance:
  1. A government-invested institution in which the amount invested solely or jointly by the State or a local government accounts for at least 20/100 of the capital, and in which the State or the local government is the largest investor;
  2. An enterprise or organization in which the amount reinvested solely or jointly by a public institution designated and publicly notified pursuant to Articles 4 through 6 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions or by a government-invested institution under subparagraph 1, accounts for at least 20/100 of the capital, and in which the public institution or government-invested institution is the largest investor;
  3. An enterprise or organization in which the amount contributed or provided as subsidies by the State or a local government accounts for at least 20/100 of the property of the enterprise or organization, and in which the State or the local government is the largest contributor or subsidizer;
  4. An enterprise or organization which conducts affairs entrusted by the Government or a local government, or the representative or executive officer of which is appointed or approved by the State or a local government.

Article 51 (Reporting by enterprises, etc.) (1) If an institution providing employment assistance specified in subparagraphs 2 and 3 of Article 34 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "enterprise, etc.") receives notification to report the type of business, the occupational category to be filled, and other relevant information, issued by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs pursuant to Article 40(1) of the Act, the institution shall file a report within 30 days from the date of receipt such notification. In such cases, the report may be filed in conjunction with a report under Article 54(1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) Matters for which the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may request enterprises, etc. to provide explanations or submit necessary books and other documents, as required to ascertain the current status pursuant to Article 40(2) of the Act shall be as follows: <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  1. Details of changes after filing a report under paragraph (1);
  2. The current employment and working conditions of persons eligible for employment assistance;
  3. A plan for employing persons eligible for employment assistance and employees;
  4. Matters regarding the explanation of additional scores awarded pursuant to Article 35(1) through (3) of the Act.
  (3) If it is necessary to compare and verify materials provided by persons eligible for employment assistance, enterprises, etc. for the efficient administration of employment assistance, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may request State agencies, local governments, or corporations established under special Acts that retain the relevant materials to cooperate in the comparison and verification of such materials, specifying the specific details thereof. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 52 (Special employment of veterans) (1) If the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs recommends multiple persons eligible for employment assistance pursuant to the main clause of Article 41(1) of the Act, the Minister shall determine the number of persons to be employed by an enterprise, etc. which fall short of the employment ratio under Article 39 of the Act and shall recommend eligible persons up to 5 times the determined number. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) An enterprise, etc. receiving the recommendation of multiple persons eligible for employment assistance pursuant to paragraph (1) shall select a person to be employed from among recommended persons and shall notify the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs of the selection within 1 month from the date of receipt the recommendation; provided, if it is impracticable to provide notification within 1 month due to unavoidable reasons, such as the administration of an employment examination, the period may be extended by up to 2 months in consultation with the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023; Nov. 12, 2024>
  (3) If the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs orders an enterprise, etc. to employ persons eligible for employment assistance pursuant to Article 41(3) of the Act, such order shall be issued through a written notice of the special employment of veterans. In such cases, the occupational category to be filled by the enterprise, etc. shall be clearly stated. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (4) "Good cause prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 41(3)2 of the Act means any of the following cases: <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  1. Where a person eligible for employment assistance sustains an injury or suffers from a disease, each of which requires medical treatment for at least 1 month;
  2. Where an enterprise, etc. are unable to employ a person eligible for employment assistance due to urgent managerial reasons, such as workforce reductions or suspension or closure of business operations;
  3. Where good cause is recognized by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs.
  (5) An enterprise, etc. that receive a written notice of the special employment of veterans pursuant to paragraph (3) shall employ a person eligible for employment assistance, as ordered by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, within 30 days from the date of receipt the notice. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (6) An employment notice for a person eligible for employment assistance under Article 41(4) of the Act shall be provided through a written employment notice.

Article 53 (Restrictions on employment assistance) (1) The period for restricting employment assistance under Article 42(2) of the Act shall be determined in accordance with the following criteria:
  1. Where the relevant person falls under Article 42(2)1 of the Act: 6 months from the date the person indicates his or her intention not to be employed;
  2. Where the relevant falls under Article 42(2)2 of the Act: 6 months from the date the person resigns;
  3. Where the relevant person falls under Article 42(2)3 of the Act: 1 year from the date the person is dismissed under disciplinary action.
  (2) "Good cause" in Article 42(2)1 and 2 of the Act shall be any of the following cases: <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  1. Where the relevant person sustains an injury or suffers from a disease, each of which requires medical treatment for at least 1 month;
  2. Where the relevant person abandons employment with an enterprise, etc. that have received a written notice of the special employment of veterans due to reasons such as workforce reductions or suspension of business operations of the relevant enterprise, etc., or where the person resigns or is dismissed due to urgent managerial reasons of the enterprise, etc.;
  3. Where the relevant person fails to pass an employment physical examination;
  4. Where wages have been in arrears for at least 3 months;
  5. Where reasonable grounds are recognized by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, such as where a person eligible for employment assistance lacks the skills or qualifications required for the occupational category in which the person intends to work or is currently employed.
  (3) "Period prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 42(2)2 of the Act means 6 months.

Article 54 (Determination of passing employment physical examination) (1) The determination of passing an employment physical examination of a soldier, police officer, or public official wounded in a disaster under Article 43 of the Act shall be made by a hospital under Article 3(2)3a of the Medical Service Act and a general hospital under item f of that subparagraph. <Amended on Nov. 12, 2024>
  (2) The head of a medical institution under paragraph (1) shall not assess unfavorably the ability of a person eligible for employment assistance to perform duties solely on the grounds of physical limitations resulting from the existing injury.

Article 55 (Standards for aggregating military service period) If an enterprise, etc. preferentially employ a person eligible for employment assistance, at least 30 percent of the person's military service period may be aggregated into his or her total career period for determining the pay grade, pursuant to Article 44 of the Act; provided, if any institution providing employment assistance specified in the subparagraphs of Article 39(2) of the Act preferentially employs such an eligible person, the service period may be aggregated by applying mutatis mutandis Articles 8 and 9 of the Public Officials Remuneration Regulations.

Article 56 (Notification of results of corrective measures for discriminatory treatment) Notification of the results of corrective measures for discriminatory treatment under Article 45(3) of the Act shall be provided within 30 days from the date of receipt a request for such measures.

Article 57 (Notification of employment events) If any event specified in the subparagraphs of Article 46 of the Act occurs, an institution providing employment assistance shall notify the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs of the details of such event within 10 days from the date of its occurrence. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 58 (Vocational rehabilitation training and vocational skills development training) (1) Vocational rehabilitation training shall be provided to soldiers, police officers, and public officials wounded in disasters pursuant to Article 48(1) of the Act, with selected subjects that are necessary for employment in a workplace or self-employment appropriate to their physical capabilities. In such cases, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall determine the procedures for selecting training subjects and other matters necessary for such training. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) If a person eligible for employment assistance seeks to receive vocational skills development training, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall recommend the person to a vocational skills development training establishment, as a person eligible for preferential vocational skills development training pursuant to Article 48(2) of the Act, by a recommendation letter for such a person in the form prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 59 (Payment of incentives for employment skills development) (1) The scope of persons eligible for incentives for employment skills development or for subsidies to cover expenses incurred in such development under Article 49(1) of the Act shall be as follows: <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  1. A person eligible for incentives for employment skills development:
  a. A person eligible for employment assistance who receives vocational skills development training at a vocational skills development training establishment under Article 48(2) of the Act;
  b. A person eligible for employment assistance who receives vocational guidance, etc. at an employment security office defined in subparagraph 1 of Article 2-2 of the Employment Security Act;
  2. A person eligible for subsidies to cover expenses incurred in employment skills development: A person eligible for employment assistance who receives vocational skills development training at a vocational skills development training establishment determined by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs to develop qualifications or skills necessary for employment.
  (2) If the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs grants an incentive for employment skills development or a subsidy to cover expenses incurred in such development pursuant to paragraph (1), the Minister may request a vocational skills development training establishment or a regional office of employment and labor to submit necessary materials to verify whether a person eligible for employment assistance has received vocational skills development training or vocational guidance, etc. In such cases, an institution requested to submit materials shall comply therewith, unless there is a compelling reason not to do so. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (3) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) and (2), matters necessary to grant incentives for employment skills development or subsidies to cover expenses incurred in such development shall be determined by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

CHAPTER V MEDICAL ASSISTANCE AND OTHER FORMS OF ASSISTANCE

Article 60 (Medical treatment) (1) Medical treatment for soldiers and police officers wounded in disasters (hereafter in this Chapter referred to as "persons eligible for medical treatment") shall be provided in accordance with the following classifications, and inpatient treatment shall be provided by a veterans hospital under Article 7 of the Korea Veterans Health Service Act (hereinafter referred to as "veterans hospital"), except in unavoidable circumstances: <Amended on Aug. 4, 2020>
  1. Emergency medical treatment: Medical treatment provided to a patient who is deemed unable to survive or at risk of suffering serious complications without immediate and necessary treatment in the event of an unexpected disaster or other emergency;
  2. Inpatient treatment: Medical treatment provided through hospitalization in a medical establishment;
  3. Outpatient treatment: Medical treatment provided on a nonhospitalized basis, allowing a patient to visit a medical establishment.
  (2) The State may entrust the medical treatment of persons eligible for medical assistance to a private medical institution established under Article 3 of the Medical Service Act, other than medical establishments operated by the State or a local government.
  (3) If a person eligible for medical treatment receives medical treatment at a medical establishment of a local government pursuant to the proviso of Article 51(3) of the Act, the local government shall bear 50 percent of the relevant medical expenses.

Article 61 (Entrustment of medical treatment following designation of medical establishments) (1) If there is no veterans hospital or private medical institution entrusted with medical treatment (hereinafter referred to as "entrusted hospital") pursuant to Article 51(2) of the Act in a Si (including the Special Metropolitan City, a Metropolitan City, a Special Self-Governing City, and Jeju Special Self-Governing Province) or Gun where a person eligible for medical treatment resides (including where the relevant medical specialty is not provided by a veterans hospital and an entrusted hospital), the person may request the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs to authorize the entrustment of medical treatment, following the designation of a medical establishment, other than a veterans hospital or an entrusted hospital; provided, a tertiary hospital under Article 3-4 of the Medical Service Act shall be excluded from medical establishments for which such request for the entrustment of medical treatment may be made. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) Upon receipt of a request under paragraph (1), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall, without delay, notify the relevant person eligible for medical treatment of the decision whether to authorize the entrustment of medical treatment. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (3) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), if a medical emergency prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs occurs, a person eligible for medical treatment may receive emergency medical care under Article 60(1)1 at a medical institution under Article 3 of the Medical Service Act. In such cases, the person, his or her guardian, or any other relevant person shall notify the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs within 14 days from the date of hospitalization, except in unavoidable circumstances prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
