  (4) If a person eligible for medical treatment is diagnosed from a medical diagnosis as a special patient prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, with a disease such as pulmonary tuberculosis, Hansen's disease, or mental disease, the head of the relevant veterans hospital may transfer the person for medical treatment to a medical establishment specializing in the treatment of such special patients, in consultation with the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (5) Necessary matters regarding the standards for entrustment to an entrusted hospital under Article 51(2) of the Act and the detailed standards, procedures, etc. for entrustment of medical treatment under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be determined by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 62 (Amount of medical expenses to be borne by patients) (1) "Injury grade prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 51(4) of the Act means Injury Grade VI.
  (2) If a person eligible for medical treatment, assigned Injury Grade VII, receives medical treatment for a disease other than the existing injury pursuant to Article 51(4) of the Act and paragraph (1) of this Article, the person shall bear 10/100 of the medical expenses to be charged to him or her, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs; provided, if the person receives emergency medical treatment under Article 60(1)1 due to a medical emergency, the State shall bear the total relevant expenses. <Amended on Dec. 29, 2017; Aug. 4, 2020; Oct. 19, 2021; May 23, 2023>
  [Title Amended on Oct. 19, 2021]

Article 63 (Reduction of, or exemption from, medical expenses) (1) If medical treatment is provided to the spouse of a person eligible for veterans' compensation pursuant to Article 51(5) of the Act, the head of the relevant veterans hospital may exempt the medical expenses or may reduce such expenses by up to 60 percent, as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) The reduction of, or exemption from, medical expenses under Article 51(6) of the Act shall be 60/100 of the expenses to be borne by any person aged 75 or older specified in the subparagraphs of Article 51(6) of the Act (excluding the costs of prescription drugs specified in subparagraph 1c of Appendix 2 of the Enforcement Decree of the National Health Insurance Act) in accordance with the percentage and amount of the expenses to be borne by the person, out of the costs of health care benefits specified in that Table. <Amended on Oct. 19, 2021>
  (3) Notwithstanding (2), if any person aged 75 or older specified in the subparagraphs of Article 51(6) of the Act is required to bear the costs of health care benefits pursuant to subparagraph 6 of Appendix 2 of the Enforcement Decree of the National Health Insurance Act, the medical expenses under Article 51(6) of the Act shall not be reduced or exempted. <Amended on Apr. 28, 2014; Dec. 24, 2019; Oct. 19, 2021>
  (4) The reduction of, or exemption from, medical expenses under the latter part of Article 51-3 of the Act shall be prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, not exceeding 60/100 of the expenses to be borne by the spouse of a person eligible for veterans' compensation. <Added on Oct. 19, 2021, May 23, 2023>
  [Title Amended on Oct. 19, 2021]

Article 64 (Bearing costs of prescription drugs) (1) If a person eligible for medical treatment or his or her family, whether bereaved or not, is dispensed with drugs at a pharmacy registered under Article 20 of the Pharmaceutical Affairs Act, based on a prescription issued by a doctor of a medical establishment or institution under Articles 51(1), (2), or (5) or 51-3 of the Act, the State shall bear the total cost of prescription drugs or the amount equivalent to the reduction or exemption rate. <Amended on Oct. 19, 2021>
  (2) Expenses to be borne by the State pursuant to paragraph (1) shall be paid by being earmarked in the budget of the Korea Veterans Health Service established under the Korea Veterans Health Service Act.

Article 64-2 (Persons not assigned injury grade eligible for medical assistance) Persons eligible for medical assistance under Article 51-2 of the Act shall be those who, following a physical examination conducted by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs pursuant to Article 6 of the Act, have not been assigned an injury grade and therefore do not fall under any of the following categories: <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  1. A soldier or police officer wounded in a disaster, as specified in Article 2(1)2 of the Act;
  2. A public official wounded in a disaster, as specified in Article 2(1)4 of the Act.
  [This Article Added on Nov. 29, 2016]

Article 65 (Prosthetic devices) (1) A prosthetic device under Article 52 is an artificial device that replaces, restores, or supplements a physical disability or loss of function of a person eligible for medical treatment, and the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall determine the duration for which each type of prosthetic device may be used. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) The manufacture of prosthetic devices under paragraph (1) and other necessary matters shall be determined by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 66 (Provision of prosthetic devices) (1) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall provide prosthetic devices to persons in need of such devices pursuant to Article 52 of the Act in accordance with the standards determined by the Minister. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) If a person provided with a prosthetic device pursuant to paragraph (1) needs repairs due to the wear and tear or malfunction of the device, the person may request the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs to repair it. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 66-2 (Details and methods of provision of psychological rehabilitation services) (1) The details of the psychological rehabilitation services provided by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs under Article 53-3(1) of the Act (hereafter in this Article referred to as "psychological rehabilitation services") shall be as follows: <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  1. Psychological counseling and tests;
  2. Arrangement of medical treatment, etc. at a mental health improvement facility defined in subparagraph 4 of Article 3 of the Act on the Improvement of Mental Health and the Support for Welfare Services for Mental Patients;
  3. Education for improving mental health;
  4. Other services prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, as deemed necessary for psychological stability and social adaptation.
  (2) A person who intends to receive psychological rehabilitation services shall file an application with the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, as prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  [This Article Added on Oct. 19, 2021]

Article 67 (Methods and scope of medical assistance) Except as provided in this Chapter, matters necessary for medical assistance to persons eligible for veterans' compensation and their bereaved families, etc., including the methods and scope of providing medical treatment and subsidies for medical expenses, shall be prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 67-2 (Inability to provide support) "Where the person lacks the ability to provide support as prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 54-2 of the Act means any of the following cases: <Amended on Apr. 1, 2025>
  1. Where the relevant person obligated to provide support (referring to the spouse, parents, children, and the spouses of such children, who are obligated to provide support; hereinafter the same shall apply) has any mental or physical disability as classified in the Disability Classification Table for Persons with Disabilities specified in Appendix 2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State;
  2. Where the relevant person obligated to provide support falls under any of the following categories and is currently in mandatory military service:
  a. A soldier enlisted for active service under Article 16 or 20 of the Military Service Act (including noncommissioned officers appointed without voluntary application);
  b. A full-time reserve service member called up pursuant to Article 22 of the Military Service Act;
  c. A member of an auxiliary police company, and a member of an obligatory firefighting unit who are seconded for any public service other than that in a military unit pursuant to Article 25 of the Military Service Act;
  d. A person called up to serve as social service personnel defined in Article 2(1)10 of the Military Service Act;
  e. A person called up to serve as alternative service personnel under Article 17 of the Act on Assignment to and Performance of Alternative Service;
  3. Where the whereabouts of the relevant person obligated to provide support have been unknown for at least 1 year;
  4. Where the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs deems that the relevant person obligated to provide support lacks ability to provide support due to schooling or financial hardship.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 11, 2023]

Article 67-3 (Inability to provide support) "Where the person lacks the ability to provide support as prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the main clause of Article 54-3 of the Act means any case specified in the subparagraphs of Article 67-2.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 11, 2023]

Article 67-4 (Persons eligible to use transportation facilities) (1) "Public institutions prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the provisions, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 54-4(1) of the Act means the Korea Railroad Corporation under Article 2 of the Korea Railroad Corporation Act (hereafter in this Article referred to as the "Korea Railroad Corporation") and urban railway corporations that are local public enterprises established under the Local Public Enterprise Act for conducting urban railroad business defined in subparagraph 4 of Article 2 of the Urban Railroad Act.
  (2) Pursuant to Article 54-4(1) of the Act, any of the following persons shall be allowed to use transportation facilities of the State, a local government, the Korea Railroad Corporation, or an urban railroad corporation free of charge or at a discounted rate; provided, a person who uses the transportation facilities or allows another person to use them by fraud or other improper means may be suspended from assistance in the use of the transportation facilities for 3 years:
  1. A person specified in Article 54-4(1)1 and 2 of the Act;
  2. One person who uses a transportation facility while directly protecting a person assigned Injury Grade I among those specified in Article 54-4(1)1 and 2 of the Act.
  (3) The types of transportation facilities of the State, local governments, the Korea Railroad Corporation, or urban railroad corporations that may be used free of charge or at a discounted rate pursuant to paragraph (2) and other matters necessary for the use of transportation facilities shall be determined by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs in consultation with the relevant State agencies, local governments, the Korea Railroad Corporation, or the heads of urban railroad corporations.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 11, 2023]

Article 67-5 (Assistance for admission to ancient palaces) (1) Pursuant to Article 54-5 of the Act, any of the following persons shall be allowed to use facilities, including ancient palaces or parks managed by the State or a local government, free of charge or at a discounted rate:
  1. A person eligible for veterans' compensation and his or her spouse;
  2. A person specified in Article 54-4(1)2 of the Act and his or her spouse;
  3. A person with priority in the order specified in the subparagraphs of Article 5(1) among the bereaved family members of those eligible for veterans' compensation and those specified in Article 54-4(1)2 of the Act; in such cases, if the person with priority is the father or mother of a person eligible for veterans' compensation or a person specified in Article 54-4(1)2 of the Act, the mother or father who does not have priority shall also be included;
  4. One person who assists the activities of those assigned Injury Grade I, II, or III, among those eligible for veterans' compensation and those specified in Article 54-4(1)2 of the Act.
  (2) The types of facilities that any person specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) may use free of charge or at a discounted rate, and the discounted rates shall be as specified in Appendix 9-2.
  (3) If a person specified in paragraph (1)1 through 3 intends to use a facility, including an ancient palace or park, free of charge or at a discounted rate, the person shall present a patriots and veterans registration card under Article 86(1) of this Decree or Article 101(1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Honorable Treatment of and Support for Persons of Distinguished Service to the State (including the mobile version of such a card) to the manager of the relevant facility.
  [This Article Added on Jul. 11, 2023]

CHAPTER VI LOANS

Article 68 (Interest rates on loans) The interest rates on loans under Article 60 of the Act shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, within the range from 1 to 5 percent per annum depending on types of loans categorized in the subparagraphs of Article 58 of the Act, by no later than December 31 of each year; provided, any of the following interest rates on loans shall be determined and publicly notified at an annual interest rate of up to 1 percent: <Amended on Apr. 30, 2018; Aug. 4, 2020; May 23, 2023>
  1. If a mortgage is executed over real estate pledged as security (hereinafter referred to as "secured property") pursuant to Article 63(2) and (4) of the Act, an interest rate on the outstanding loan amount during the period of the mortgage;
  2. If any loan remains unpaid following the execution of a mortgage over the secured property, an interest rate on the outstanding loan amount;
  3. If a lawsuit has been filed for the repayment of a loan against a person who obtained the loan by pledging veterans' benefits (excluding livelihood improvement allowances and lump-sum payment on death) or other security; or by providing a guarantor pursuant to Article 63(4) of the Act, an interest rate on the outstanding loan amount during the period of such lawsuit;
  4. If an extension of the maturity date of a loan is granted due to a natural disaster, accident, financial hardship, disease, or any other similar circumstance, an interest rate on the outstanding loan amount during the period of repayment deferral.

Article 69 (Application for loans) (1) A person who intends to obtain a loan pursuant to Article 61(1) of the Act shall submit an application for a loan in the form prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, and in cases of a housing loan, the application shall be accompanied by a document verifying nonhomeownership. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) Upon receipt of an application under paragraph (1), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall determine whether to provide a loan within 25 days from receipt in accordance with the criteria for determining loans under Article 61(2) of the Act and shall notify the applicant of the result. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (3) If an applicant for a loan under paragraph (1) is notified of his or her eligibility for a loan pursuant to paragraph (2), the applicant shall submit an application for loan payment to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, along with the documents prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (4) If a person eligible for a loan under Article 56 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "person eligible for a loan") intends to take out a loan for livelihood stability, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may provide such loan only upon receiving an application for the loan payment in lieu of the procedures prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (3). <Amended on Aug. 4, 2020; May 23, 2023>

Article 70 (Term of loan repayment) The term of loan repayment for each type of loan under Article 62(1) of the Act shall be as follows; provided, if it is deemed necessary by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, the term may be adjusted by loan type: <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  1. A loan for purchasing farmland: 12 years after the 3-year grace period;
  2. A housing loan:
  a. A loan for purchasing housing or a site, or for the construction of new housing: 20 years;
  b. A housing improvement loan and housing rent loan: 7 years;
  3. A loan for operation of business: 10 years;
  4. A loan for livelihood stabilization: 5 years.

Article 71 (Application for extension of term of repayment) (1) A person who intends to obtain an extension of the maturity date of a loan pursuant to Article 62(2) of the Act shall submit an application for the extension of the term of loan repayment to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, along with the documents prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) Upon receipt of an application under paragraph (1), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall without delay determine whether to grant the extension and shall notify the applicant of the determination. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 72 (Lump-sum loan repayment) If a person who has obtained a loan uses it for purposes other than the original one, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall require the person to repay the outstanding loan principal and interest in a lump sum pursuant to Article 62(3) of the Act; provided, if lump-sum repayment is deemed impracticable due to financial hardship or other similar reasons, the Minister may allow the repayment to be made in installments over a period of up to 3 years. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 73 (Interest rates applied due to delayed repayment of loan principal) (1) If a person liable to repay a loan pursuant to Article 62 of the Act delays repayment, overdue interest may be applied to the loan principal amount for which repayment has been delayed. In such cases, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall determine the overdue interest rate, which shall not exceed the lowest overdue interest rate applied by banks on loans as of January 1 of each year. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) Notwithstanding the former part of paragraph (1), if repayment is made in a lump sum or in installments under Article 72, no overdue interest shall be applied to the portion of the loan principal that has not yet reached its repayment deadline under the original loan agreement, among the loan principal amount for which repayment has been delayed.

Article 74 (Appointment of appraisers) (1) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall appoint appraisers from among public officials under his or her jurisdiction to appraise secured property, housing constructed for persons eligible for loans, sites secured for such construction, and secured property purchased pursuant to Article 66(1) of the Act. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) Qualifications of appraisers under paragraph (1), the criteria for determination of appraised prices, and other necessary matters shall be determined by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 75 (Replacement of secured property) (1) A person who intends to replace secured property pursuant to Article 63(6) or (7) of the Act shall submit an application for replacement of secured property to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, along with the documents prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) Upon receipt of an application under paragraph (1), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall determine whether to approve the application within 5 days from receipt and shall notify the applicant of the determination. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (3) A person who obtains approval of replacing secured property under paragraph (2) due to the unavoidable sale of farmland or a house acquired through a loan and the subsequent purchase of real estate for the same purpose shall follow the procedures for providing security under Article 63(2) of the Act for the property to be substituted.
  (4) Upon completion of the procedures under paragraph (3), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall proceed with the procedures for canceling, etc., the mortgage under Article 63(8) of the Act for the property initially provided as security. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 76 (Assumption of obligations) (1) If a person eligible for a loan who is a successful bidder intends to assume the obligation to repay a loan on the secured property in lieu of paying the purchase price of the secured property of another person eligible for a loan, which has been put up for auction, the person shall submit an application for approval to assume obligations to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs pursuant to Article 65(1) of the Act. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) Upon receipt of an application under paragraph (1), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall determine whether to grant approval and shall notify the applicant of the determination. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 77 (Purchase price of secured property) (1) If secured property put up for auction pursuant to Article 66(1) of the Act is to be purchased, the purchase price of the secured property shall be the price determined by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, within the limits of the loan amount on the secured property, based on the current market value. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) If the property purchased pursuant to paragraph (1) is disposed of, the disposal price shall be the price determined by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, based on the current market value at the time of the disposal. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (3) If deemed necessary when determining the purchase price and disposal price under paragraphs (1) and (2), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may request an authorized appraisal and assessment institution to conduct the appraisal. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 78 (Disposal of purchased property) (1) If the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs purchases secured property put up for auction pursuant to Article 66 of the Act, the Minister may lease the purchased property until it is disposed of or may appoint a manager to manage the purchased property until it is disposed of or leased. In such cases, the Minister may pay the manager remuneration and expenses incurred in maintaining and preserving the property under management, within the budget. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) The purchased property under paragraph (1) shall be disposed of through a general competitive tendering procedure; provided, if such property is leased and disposed of to the lessee, the disposal may be conducted through a private contract.
  (3) The full amount of the disposal price of the purchased property shall be paid in a lump sum; provided, if the purchased property is sold to a person eligible for a loan, the person may pay the disposal price, plus the interest determined by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, for which the interest rate shall not exceed 5 percent per annum, in installments over a period of up to 5 years. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 79 (Reporting of succession to loans) Upon the death of a person who has obtained a loan, if the heir intends to report succession to the loan obligations pursuant to Article 67(2) of the Act, the heir shall submit a report on the succession to obligations to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, along with the documents prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, within 3 months from the date of inheritance. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 80 (Notification of payment) If the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs requires a person to pay the principal of and interest on the loan, the disposal price of the purchased property, etc., the Minister shall issue a payment notice to the person subject to the payment. In such cases, the Minister shall without delay issue a demand for payment thereof to a person who fails to make the payment by the deadline. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 80-2 (Preferential supply of housing) (1) If houses constructed and supplied by the State, a local government, or a project entity constructing and supplying privately constructed housing pursuant to Article 54 of the Housing Act (hereafter in this Article referred to as "housing supplier") are preferentially supplied to persons specified in the subparagraphs of Article 67-2(1) of the Act (hereafter in this Article referred to as "persons eligible for preferential supply of houses") pursuant to paragraph (1) or (2) of that Article, the detailed procedures and methods for such supply shall be governed by the Housing Act. <Amended on Aug. 4, 2020; Jul. 11, 2023>
  (2) If a housing supplier preferentially supplies houses to persons eligible for preferential supply of houses under paragraph (1), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall select persons eligible for such supply from among the applicants referred to in the former part of Article 67-2(3) of the Act according to the quantity of houses to be supplied and the criteria determined by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, in consideration of such factors as the period of nonhomeownership, the standard of living, and the degree of sacrifice and contribution, and shall recommend such selected persons to the housing supplier. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  [This Article Added on Apr. 30, 2018]

CHAPTER VII SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS AND PENALTY PROVISIONS

Article 81 (Recovery of veterans' benefits) (1) When making a disposition to recover veterans' benefits, etc. under the main clause, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 68(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "veterans' benefits") and any interest thereon (hereinafter referred to as "amount to be recovered") pursuant to that paragraph (hereafter in this Article referred to as "recovery disposition"), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall send a notice requiring the return of the amount to be recovered to a person who has received the veterans' benefits, etc. (including his or her heir and excluding persons exempted from duty to return veterans' benefits pursuant to Article 69 of the act; hereafter in this Article referred to as "person liable to pay"). In such cases, the person liable to pay shall return the amount to be recovered within 30 days of receiving such notice.
  (2) "Interest prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the main clause, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 68(1) of the Act means the amount calculated by multiplying the veterans' benefits by the interest rate specified in subparagraph 1 and the period specified in subparagraph 2:
  1. The interest rate: The interest rate specified in the main clause of Article 43-3(2) of the Enforcement Decree of the Framework Act on National Taxes;
  2. The period: The number of months beginning with the month in which the veterans' benefits, etc. are received and ending with the month immediately preceding the month in which the notice of recovery disposition is provided; provided, if the veterans' benefits, etc. are returned before such notice is provided, the period shall be the number of months beginning with the month in which the veterans' benefits, etc. are received and ending with the month immediately preceding the month in which all the benefits, etc. are returned.
  (3) The limit on property acquired through inheritance under the proviso, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 68(1) of the Act shall be calculated in pursuant to Article 11(1) of the Enforcement Decree of the Framework Act on National Taxes.
  (4) The amount of arrears under Article 68(2) of the Act (hereafter in this Article referred to as "amount of arrears") shall be the amount calculated by multiplying the overdue veterans' benefits, etc. by an interest rate of 5/100 per year for the period from the day after the payment due date (in cases of installment payments under paragraph (5) of this Article, referring to the due date of each installment payment; and in cases of revocation of the installment payment determination under paragraph (7), referring to the date of revoking the installment payment for the installment payments not yet due before the revocation) to the day before the full payment of the amount to be recovered. In such cases, the period for collecting the amount of arrears shall not exceed 60 months.
  (5) If a person liable to pay intends to pay the amount to be recovered in installments, the person shall submit an application for installment payments of the amount to be recovered to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs by the due date specified in the latter part of paragraph (1), as prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. In such cases, if the Minister determines to approve such installment payments, the payments may be made in monthly installments, the number of which does not exceed the limit specified in the following, beginning with the month following the month in which the determination is made:
  1. If the amount to be returned is less than 10 million won: 20 installments;
  2. If the amount to be returned is at least 10 million won but less than 20 million won: 40 installments;
  3. If the amount to be returned is at least 20 million won: 60 installments.
  (6) In cases of installment payments under paragraph (5), the interest thereon and the amount of each installment shall be as follows; provided, in cases falling under Article 68(1)3 of the Act, if the veterans' benefits were paid erroneously from the beginning due to a mistake or omission by the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, the interest on the installment payments shall be exempted:
  1. Interest on installment payments: Calculated by multiplying the amount of veterans' benefits, etc. payable during the installment payment period by the interest rate specified in paragraph (2)1;
  2. The amount of each installment payment: The amount to be recovered and the interest on the installment payment specified in subparagraph 1, divided equally by the number of installments.
  (7) If a person liable to pay fails to make installment payments on at least 3 consecutive occasions (including partial payments), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may revoke the determination of installment payments and collect the remaining amount to be recovered, along with the interest and the amount of arrears accrued up to that point, in a lump sum.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 11, 2023]

Article 82 (Write-off) If the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs intends to make a write-off disposition pursuant to Article 68(4) of the Act, a resolution to that effect shall be adopted by the Patriots and Veterans Entitlement Commission. <Amended on May 23, 2023; Jul. 11, 2023>

Article 83 (Grounds for exemption from obligations to return veterans' benefits) (1) Cases where a person is allowed to be exempted from the obligation to return veterans' benefits, etc. pursuant to Article 69 of the Act shall be any of the following cases:
  1. Where the name, rank, military number, place of registration, date or area of death or injury, or any similar information of a person notified as a deceased or injured person in the course of official duties differs from the information notified in military or police records;
  2. Where the classification of death and discharge from military service of a person notified as a deceased or injured person in the course of official duties is corrected and notified as a person who died or was injured due to any reason other than official duties;
  3. Where a person notified as a deceased person in the course of official duties returns alive or is confirmed to be alive;
  4. Where it is impossible to confirm the death or injury of a person notified as a deceased or injured person in the course of official duties based on military or police records;
  5. Where it is verified that a person who has received compensation under the Act fails to meet the requirements for registration as a person eligible for veterans' compensation, due to reasons not attributable to the person.
  (2) If the grounds for exemption from the obligation to return veterans' benefits, etc. under paragraph (1) arise, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall examine and verify such grounds without delay; and if the Minister intends to grant an exemption from such obligation, a resolution to that effect shall be adopted by the Patriots and Veterans Entitlement Commission. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 83-2 (Request for provision of materials) The specific scope of materials or information that the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may request from the head of a relevant agency under Article 70(1) of the Act shall be as specified in Appendix 9-3. <Amended on May 23, 2023; Jul. 11, 2023>
  [This Article Added on Apr. 30, 2018]

Article 84 (Demeaning conduct) (1) "Demeaning conduct prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Articles 71(1) and 72(1)5 of the Act means any of the following acts:
  1. Coercing another person to grant an unfair advantage or assisting another person in obtaining such advantage by exploiting the status of a person eligible for veterans' compensation;
  2. Interfering with the execution of public duties through assault, intimidation, property damage, or any other unjustifiable means.
  (2) "Crimes prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 71(2) of the Act means crimes prescribed in the Criminal Act; provided, the foregoing shall not apply if a crime is committed by negligence.

Article 85 (Determination of persons subject to suspension of compensation) (1) If the Patriots and Veterans Entitlement Commission intends to adopt a resolution on any of the following matters, the Commission shall require the relevant person to attend its meeting and shall hear his or her opinion. In such cases, if the relevant person submits his or her opinion in writing, he or she shall be deemed to have attended its meeting; and if the person fails to attend its meeting at the designated time without good cause, he or she shall be deemed to have no opinion: <Amended on Nov. 11, 2014>
  1. Suspension of compensation under Article 71(1) of the Act;
  2. Exclusion of the relevant person from those subject to the application of the Act under 72(1)5 of the Act;
  3. Determination to register a person excluded from the application of the Act as a person eligible for the application of the Act under Article 72(3) of the Act.
  (2) If matters regarding paragraph (1) are deliberated and resolved on, the chairperson of the Patriots and Veterans Entitlement Commission shall notify the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs of the result without delay. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (3) Upon receipt of a notification of the result under paragraph (2), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall make a determination on the matters specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) within 20 days and shall notify the relevant person of the result. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 86 (Issuance of patriots and veterans registration cards) (1) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall issue a patriots and veterans registration card (including the mobile version of such a card; hereinafter the same shall apply) to persons eligible for veterans' compensation and bereaved family members with priority registered pursuant to Article 4(3) of the Act. In such cases, if a bereaved family member with priority is the father or mother of a person eligible for veterans' compensation, such a card shall also be issued to a mother or father who is not a bereaved family member with priority.
  (2) A person who has been issued with a patriots and veterans registration card pursuant to paragraph (1) may file an application for reissuance of such a card with the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, in any of the following cases:
  1. Where the patriots and veterans registration card becomes unusable due to loss or damage;
  2. Where there is a change in any matter prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs among the details entered in the patriots and veterans registration card, such as the name and date of birth.
  (3) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may establish and operate an information system for the issuance, reissuance, management, and authentication of patriots and veterans registration cards and other relevant processes. In such cases, the operating system commonly applicable to identity verification under Article 12(4) of the Enforcement Decree of the Electronic Government Act may be utilized for the issuance, reissuance, management, and authentication of the mobile version of patriots and veterans registration cards.
  (4) Upon receipt of an application from a person eligible for veterans' compensation registered pursuant to Article 4(3) of the Act or his or her family member, whether bereaved or not, the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs may issue a document verifying that the relevant person is a person eligible for veterans' compensation or his or her family member, whether bereaved or not.
  (5) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (4), matters necessary for the issuance, re-issuance, etc. of a registration certificate of a person entitled to veterans benefits shall be prescribed by Decree of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on May 23, 2023]

Article 87 (Procedures for payment of monetary awards) (1) A person who intends to file a report regarding any person engaged in fraud as specified in the subparagraphs of Article 73(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "person engaged in fraud") shall submit a report of fraud to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, along with the documents prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (2) Upon receipt of a report under paragraph (1), the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall examine the facts related to a person engaged in fraud and shall notify the person who has filed the report regarding the person engaged in fraud of the result. <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (3) To receive a monetary award, a person who has filed a report regarding a person engaged in fraud shall submit an application for payment of a monetary award to the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, along with the documents prescribed by Ministerial Decree of Patriots and Veterans Affairs, after receiving a notification under paragraph (2). <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  (4) The Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs shall pay a monetary award within 30 days from the date of an application for payment of the monetary award, unless there is a compelling reason not to do so. <Amended on May 23, 2023>

Article 88 (Criteria for payment of monetary awards) (1) A monetary award under Article 73(1) of the Act shall be paid, within the range of up to 3 million won per case, according to the following classifications:
  1. If the amount of veterans' benefits received fraudulently is at least 5 million won: An amount equivalent to 10/100 of the amount of the veterans' benefits received fraudulently;
  2. Where the amount of the monetary award fraudulently obtained is less than 5 million won or none at all: 500,000 won.
  (2) The annual limit on monetary awards paid to each person pursuant to paragraph (1) (for the period from January 1 to December 31) shall be 15 million won.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 29, 2016]

Article 89 (Methods of payment of monetary awards for concurrent reports) (1) If at least 2 persons jointly file a report regarding the same fraud, a monetary award shall be distributed equally among them; provided, if persons entitled to receive a monetary award agree in advance on the method of distribution and file an application for payment, the award shall be paid in accordance with the agreed method.
  (2) If at least 2 reports are filed regarding the same fraud, a monetary award shall be paid to the person who first filed the report.

Article 90 (Restrictions on payment of monetary awards) A monetary award need not be paid in any of the following cases: <Amended on May 23, 2023>
  1. Where the details of the reported fraud have already been disclosed in the media or are already under examination or investigation;
  2. Where a person who has filed a report regarding a fraud is a public official or an employee of the Ministry of Patriots and Veterans Affairs;
  3. In cases of a report regarding a person specified in Article 73(1)2 of the Act, where 3 months have not passed from the last day of the month in which the date the relevant rights were extinguished;
  4. Where the Minister of Patriots and Veterans Affairs deems it appropriate not to pay a monetary award.
